element: ArtifactCopilot (Wu et al. 2026, Agent-Based Software Artifact Evaluation; incl. ArtifactGuide rubric)

UC1.note: Output is a reviewer-facing review report with badge verdicts, not a venue-format artifact appendix.

UC3.evidence: a Functional badge decision cites the workflow execution log from dimension D3 and the claim mapping file from dimension D4. All references include hyperlinks to the corresponding run directories (Sec IV.D, p6)
UC3.note: Claim-to-output mapping (D4, RW4) is produced, but as internal evidence for the badge decision, not as a standalone claims->components deliverable; 1 is right.

UC4.evidence: For every score from dimension D1 to D5, the report enumerates the specific checklist items from ARTIFACTGUIDE that were satisfied or violated. Each item is directly linked to the corresponding command output (Sec IV.D, p6)
UC4.note: Report lists violated checklist items per dimension plus severity-ranked flags relative to an explicit ACM-grounded rubric; arguably 2 rather than 1, though the audience is reviewers and the standard is the authors' own rubric.

UC5.note: Weak claim mapping (D4 WR) is scored as an artifact deficit, not as paper underspecification; nothing checks the paper itself.

UC6.note: Sec VI.B gives prose design guidance for artifacts but the tool generates no artifact material.

UC7.note: Judgment is against the rubric, never against exemplar (P,A) pairs.

B1.evidence: it should be designed as a reviewer-oriented evidence assistant that makes route choices explicit, records intervention burden ... and localizes where human adjudication is still needed (Sec VI.A, p10)
B1.note: Sec VI.B mentions it can double as a 'detector of artifact quality' for authors, but the design and user study are reviewer-facing.

B2.evidence: E2: reviewer runs representative workflow and obtains valid output; E3: reviewer runs full or near-full main workflow and obtains paper-facing result objects (Table II, p4)
B2.note: Only reviewer-executed evidence (E2+) counts toward badges; environment reconstruction and workflow execution are core phases.

B3.evidence: the input to ARTIFACTCOPILOT is the paper and its corresponding artifacts (Sec IV.A, p5)
B3.note: Both are inputs, but the phase sequence (availability gate, docs, environment, execution) is repo-driven; the paper is consulted mainly for D4 claim mapping.

B4.evidence: Badge rules: Available: GC1-GC3 pass; Functional: Available, D2-D4 >= WA, E2 or above, no I4; Reusable: Functional, both D1 and D5 >= WA, transfer validation succeeds, no I4 (Table II, p4)
B4.note: Whole system is driven by an explicit published rubric (ArtifactGuide) grounded in ACM badging policy and ICSE/ASE/FSE/ISSTA guidelines, with deterministic badge derivation; 5 fits better than 4.

B5.evidence: The final phase produces a structured review report in both Markdown and JSON formats ... For each Available, Functional, and Reusable badge, the report explicitly states the deterministic rule applied (Sec IV.D, p6)
B5.note: Headline output and evaluation metric is the badge (plus R/WR/WA/A scores); the accompanying report is structured evidence, not prose, so 2 holds, though 3 is arguable given RQ4 studies the report.

disagreements: UC4: current 1, should be 2 because the report is a deliverable that enumerates, per dimension D1-D5, the ArtifactGuide checklist items violated (with linked evidence) and lists consistency flags by severity, i.e. it reports what the package lacks relative to an explicit ACM-grounded standard (Sec IV.D, p6).

B4: current 4, should be 5 because the agent is entirely driven by an explicit published rubric (ArtifactGuide, grounded in ACM v1.1 policy and four venues' AE guidelines) and derives badges via deterministic rules (Table II, p4); the paper's thesis is that AE needs this explicit standard.
one_line_summary: Reviewer-facing agent that executes an artifact through a fixed phase sequence under the ArtifactGuide rubric and emits ACM badge verdicts with an evidence-linked structured report.
